chapters.title: Cyrus permits the return and restores the vessels

parts.text: The LORD stirs Cyrus of Persia to issue a proclamation fulfilling his word through Jeremiah. Cyrus declares that God has charged him to build a house in Jerusalem and invites God’s people to return for that work. Those remaining are to assist with money, goods, animals, and freewill offerings. Family leaders, priests, and Levites whose spirits God has moved prepare to go.

Cyrus also returns the temple vessels that Nebuchadnezzar removed to Babylon. They are counted and entrusted to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah. The chapter lists kinds of gold and silver vessels and records their return with the captives to Jerusalem.

chapters.title: The returning families and their gifts

parts.text: The chapter lists the families and towns represented among those returning from Babylon with Zerubbabel and the other leaders. It separately records priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, Nethinims, and descendants of Solomon’s servants, showing the different households and duties within the restored community.

Some returnees cannot establish their ancestry. Priestly claimants without a genealogical record are excluded from the most holy food until the matter can be settled through a priest with Urim and Thummim. The congregation totals 42,360, besides servants and singers. Animals and contributions are recorded, and family heads give toward rebuilding God’s house according to their ability. The people settle in their cities.

chapters.title: The altar is restored and the foundation laid

parts.text: The people gather in Jerusalem in the seventh month. Jeshua and Zerubbabel restore the altar and begin the prescribed offerings despite fear of neighboring peoples. They keep the feast of tabernacles and resume regular sacrifices before the temple’s foundation is laid. Workers and timber are obtained for the rebuilding.

In the second year, Levites oversee the work as the builders lay the foundation. Priests and singers praise the LORD for his goodness and enduring mercy, and the people shout for joy. Older men who saw the former house weep aloud. The cries of joy and grief mingle so loudly that they cannot be distinguished and are heard far away.

Adversaries offer to join the temple rebuilding, claiming that they also worship Israel’s God. Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the family heads refuse, affirming their responsibility under Cyrus’s command. The surrounding people then discourage the builders and hire counselors to frustrate the work through the years that follow.

The chapter also records accusations during the reigns of Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes. A letter portrays Jerusalem as rebellious and warns that rebuilding its walls will threaten royal revenues and authority. Artaxerxes orders the city’s work stopped until further permission, and officials enforce this by force. The account closes by noting that temple work remained halted until Darius’s second year.

chapters.title: Prophetic encouragement and an official inquiry

parts.text: Haggai and Zechariah prophesy to the returned community in God’s name. Encouraged and helped by them, Zerubbabel and Jeshua resume building the temple. Tatnai and other officials question their authority and ask who leads the work, but God watches over the elders, and construction continues while the matter is referred to Darius.

The officials report the Jews’ explanation: their fathers’ sins brought the temple’s destruction and exile, but Cyrus authorized rebuilding and returned its vessels. They name Sheshbazzar as the governor who received those vessels and laid the foundation. Tatnai asks Darius to search the royal records and confirm whether Cyrus issued the decree.

chapters.title: Darius confirms the decree and the temple is finished

parts.text: A search uncovers Cyrus’s decree at Achmetha, confirming the rebuilding, royal payment, and return of temple vessels. Darius orders the officials to leave the builders alone and provide expenses and sacrificial supplies from royal revenues. He also threatens severe punishment for anyone who alters the decree and invokes God’s judgment on those who would destroy the house.

The elders prosper through the prophets’ ministry and complete the temple in Darius’s sixth year. They dedicate it with joy, offer twelve goats for all Israel, and arrange priestly and Levitical service according to Moses’ book. The returned people and others who separate from uncleanness keep passover and unleavened bread with gladness.

Ezra is introduced as a priest descended from Aaron and a skilled scribe in Moses’ law. In Artaxerxes’ seventh year he travels from Babylon to Jerusalem with other Israelites and temple servants. God’s good hand is upon him. He has prepared his heart to study the LORD’s law, obey it, and teach it in Israel.

Artaxerxes authorizes willing Israelites to accompany Ezra and supplies gifts, temple vessels, and access to further provisions. Temple servants receive tax exemption. Ezra is empowered to appoint judges, teach the law, and enforce it with stated penalties. He praises God for moving the king to honor the temple and granting him favor before the royal court.

chapters.title: Ezra’s company seeks protection for the journey

parts.text: Ezra records the families traveling with him. At the gathering by Ahava, he discovers that no Levites are present and sends men to obtain ministers for the temple. Levites and Nethinims join them. Ezra proclaims a fast for a safe journey, having declined to ask for military protection after declaring God’s care for those who seek him. God hears their prayer.

He weighs the sacred gifts and entrusts them to responsible men for safekeeping. God preserves the company from enemies and ambushes on the road. In Jerusalem the treasures are weighed and recorded, sacrifices are offered for Israel, and the king’s commissions are delivered to officials who assist the people and temple.

chapters.title: Ezra confesses the people’s renewed unfaithfulness

parts.text: Leaders tell Ezra that the people, including priests and Levites, have joined in the surrounding nations’ abominations and married their daughters. Rulers have taken a leading part. Ezra tears his clothes, plucks hair from his head and beard, and sits astonished. Those who tremble at God’s words gather around him until the evening sacrifice.

Ezra then confesses Israel’s accumulated guilt and the justice of its past captivity. He acknowledges the mercy that preserved a remnant and enabled the temple’s restoration under Persian rule. Their renewed disobedience after such kindness leaves them without excuse. He fears that further unfaithfulness could bring destruction with no remnant left, and acknowledges God’s righteousness.

chapters.title: The community addresses the forbidden marriages

parts.text: As Ezra weeps and confesses, a large assembly gathers in grief. Shechaniah proposes a covenant to put away the foreign wives and their children according to the law. Ezra secures an oath and summons the returned people to Jerusalem. Amid heavy rain, they agree to confess and separate, but arrange a formal inquiry because the matter is too extensive to settle at once.

The investigation identifies those who had taken foreign wives, including priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and other Israelites. Priests pledge to put away their wives and offer a ram for their trespass. The chapter names the men concerned and notes that some marriages had produced children.
